source.work: Supabase documentation, supabase-js client and API keys
source.paraphrase: The anon key is safe for the browser and obeys RLS. The service_role key bypasses RLS and must never ship to the client.

invariants.why: A service_role key in client-reachable code hands every reader full bypass of row-level security. Rotation then means reissuing keys and auditing every row.
invariants.fixHint: Build the browser client with the anon key. Move service_role use into server code and expose safe operations through routes.
invariants.avoid: Reading the key from process.env does not make it safe. A SERVICE_ROLE value in a component or page file still ships to the browser. App Router and Pages Router handlers (app/api, pages/api, and route.ts) are server-only and are not flagged.

source.work: Supabase documentation, supabase-js and ssr client setup
source.paraphrase: Browser and server clients come from @supabase/supabase-js or @supabase/ssr. The bare supabase specifier is not the client entrypoint.

invariants.why: Importing createClient from the wrong package resolves to nothing maintained, so the client silently misses auth, cookie, and typing behavior the documented packages provide.
invariants.fixHint: Import createClient from @supabase/supabase-js in the browser, or from @supabase/ssr where cookies are involved.
invariants.avoid: Dynamic import and require of the same bare specifier are the same mistake, not an escape. A string that only says supabase inside an exported function is not an import.

source.work: Supabase documentation, querying with range and limit
source.locator: pagination pages for range and limit
source.paraphrase: Reads should page with range or cap with limit. An unbounded select returns the whole result set in one call.

invariants.why: One unbounded read can pull the whole table into memory, the response, and the bill. The failure shows up in production data sizes, not in review.
invariants.fixHint: Chain .range(from, to), .limit(n), .single(), or .maybeSingle() onto a table read. A select that returns rows from insert, update, upsert, or delete is already one row set.
invariants.avoid: The rule reads a Supabase .from(...).select(...) in a file that imports @supabase/supabase-js or @supabase/ssr. .range(), .limit(), .order(), .single(), and .maybeSingle() are bounds. .csv() is not. A select that is not that chain, including Drizzle db.select().from(...) and DOM element.select(), is not this call.

source.paraphrase: The auth admin API manages users with the service_role key and bypasses RLS. It runs server-side only.

invariants.why: An admin call from the browser needs the bypass key next to it, so flagging the call also flags the key leak. Either one alone compromises every user row.
invariants.fixHint: Move admin calls into server code and call them from the client through a route that checks the caller's session first.
invariants.avoid: An invite-shaped createUser is still the admin API. getUser and session reads stay client-safe and are not flagged. App Router and Pages Router handlers (app/api, pages/api, and route.ts) are server-only and are not flagged.

source.work: Supabase documentation, Migrating to the SSR package from Auth Helpers
source.paraphrase: The Auth Helpers packages are deprecated and replaced by @supabase/ssr. Bug fixes and new features land only in @supabase/ssr, so uninstall the helpers and create clients with createBrowserClient and createServerClient.

invariants.why: The deprecated helpers no longer get fixes, so session and cookie bugs stay in the app. A new file that imports them also grows a codebase that must migrate later.
invariants.fixHint: Import createBrowserClient or createServerClient from @supabase/ssr and pass cookie getAll/setAll handlers, as in the Supabase SSR guide for your framework.
invariants.avoid: Do not wrap the helpers in a local barrel to hide the import; the re-export is still flagged. A string that names the package without importing it is not an import. @supabase/auth-ui-react and @supabase/supabase-js are different packages and stay allowed.

source.work: Supabase documentation, Setting up Server-Side Auth for Next.js (supabase.com)
source.paraphrase: Never trust supabase.auth.getSession() inside server code such as middleware, route handlers, or server actions; it does not revalidate the Auth token. Always use supabase.auth.getUser().

invariants.why: auth.getSession() reads the session cookie without revalidating its signature or revocation state with the Supabase Auth server, allowing spoofed or revoked sessions in server handlers.
invariants.fixHint: Call await supabase.auth.getUser() in server actions, route handlers, and createServerClient contexts.
invariants.avoid: Matches .auth.getSession() in files declaring HTTP route handlers (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), 'use server' directives, or createServerClient calls.
